title: Counit-normalized supported classes and degree-zero exceptional sections
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $Z,X$ be finite-type $k$-schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$; let $B_0=Ri^!_0K$ be the bounded-below right derived functor of $M\mapsto i^{-1}\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], with support counit $\epsilon_0:i_*B_0\to K$ of the support adjunction of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. Assume $C_0=B_0[2]$ is isomorphic to $A_Z[0]$ in the derived category and belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Set $B=Ri^!K$ for the finite-level transported exceptional value of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] at compactification $(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$, and put $C=B[2]$.

There is a canonical isomorphism $\phi:B_0\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ satisfying $\epsilon\circ i_*\phi=\epsilon_0$, where $\epsilon$ is the counit of the relative exceptional adjunction of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2) at the compactification $(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$. It identifies the support adjunction with the relative exceptional adjunction on every bounded-below test object of etale origin (an object isomorphic to the exact comparison pullback of an etale derived object [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]). In particular $\phi[2]$ identifies $C_0$ with $C$ and carries its degree-zero concentration, constant rank-one cohomology and finite-Tor constructibility to $C$.

Write $\chi:H^2_Z(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X,A)}(i_*A_Z,K[2])$ for the supported-Hom identification of [lem-pur-supported-hom] with $a=2$, where support cohomology is the cohomology of the derived kernel of restriction [def-pur-support-cohomology]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$\eta:H^2_Z(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}(A_Z,C).$$
Its formula is $\chi$, followed by the canonical shift identification with $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*(A_Z[-2]),K)$, the support adjunction to $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A_Z[-2],B_0)$, shifting to $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A_Z,C_0)$, and postcomposition with $\phi[2]$. It agrees with the relative exceptional adjunction on the test object $A_Z[-2]$.

Evaluation $m\mapsto\mathcal H^0(m)(1)$, using the canonical degree-zero cohomology identification of $A_Z[0]$, is an isomorphism
$$\mathrm{ev}:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Z,A)}(A_Z,C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Z,\mathcal H^0(C))$$
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Under the canonical truncation $C\cong\mathcal H^0(C)[0]$, the inverse of evaluation takes a section $v$ to the module-sheaf map $a\mapsto a\,v|_W$ on each site object $W$, followed by the inverse truncation isomorphism. Consequently $(\mathrm{ev}\eta)^{-1}$ is a canonical isomorphism from these global sections to $H^2_Z(X,K)$. For every $\alpha\in H^1(V,j^*K)$ and its boundary $\beta=\partial\alpha$ in the support long exact sequence [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], the morphism $m=\eta(\beta)$ satisfies $\mathrm{ev}(m)=\mathrm{ev}\eta(\beta)$ and $(\mathrm{ev}\eta)^{-1}(\mathrm{ev}(m))=\beta$. This assertion uses no ambient exceptional adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale inputs.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $i$ is proper, separated and finite type, so $(\mathrm{id}_Z,i)$ is the stated compactification. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] its proper part has a finite dimension bound (choose $d=0$ if $Z$ is empty). Thus [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2) gives $B\in D^+(Z,A)$ and the natural relative bijections $T_H:\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*H,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(H,B)$ for bounded-below etale-origin $H$. In this identity-open compactification $P_c=i_*$, since the latter is exact by [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. That lemma also gives the support adjunction on all bounded-below tests, with counit $\epsilon_0$.

proof.text:
Both representing objects are in the test class. Indeed $B_0\cong A_Z[-2]$ by hypothesis, and [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1),(3) gives an etale origin for this shifted constant object. Write $D=i_c^	imes R
u_{X,*}K$, so $B=
u_Z^*D$ by [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Choose a lower bound $a$ for $B$. For $r<a$, exact comparison gives $
u_Z^*\mathcal H^r(D)\cong\mathcal H^r(B)=0$. Comparison reflects zero sheaves: [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] is faithful on their degree-zero singles, so the identity of such a single is zero if its pullback is zero. Hence $\mathcal H^r(D)=0$ for $r<a$. Thus $D\in D^+$ is an origin witness for $B$. No origin for $K$ is required.

source.place: Second paragraph, supported cohomology, Hom and global sections, with the first-paragraph support-to-exceptional comparison; returned steps 7-9.

proof.text: Define $\epsilon=T_B^{-1}(1_B)$ and $\phi=T_{B_0}(\epsilon_0)$. Naturality of $T$ in the test object gives $\epsilon\circ i_*\phi=\epsilon_0$. Let $\psi:B\to B_0$ be the support-adjunction transpose of $\epsilon$, so $\epsilon_0\circ i_*\psi=\epsilon$. Consequently $\epsilon_0\circ i_*(\psi\phi)=\epsilon_0$ and $\epsilon\circ i_*(\phi\psi)=\epsilon$. The support bijection on test $B_0$ makes the first equality imply $\psi\phi=1_{B_0}$; the relative bijection on test $B$ makes the second imply $\phi\psi=1_B$. These tests are legitimate by step 2. Thus $\phi$ is an isomorphism, uniquely determined by the counit equation since $T_{B_0}$ is injective. For any allowed $H$ and $u:H\to B_0$, that equation gives $\epsilon\circ i_*(\phi u)=\epsilon_0\circ i_*u$; taking relative transposes shows that postcomposition by $\phi$ identifies the two adjunction bijections. This also proves canonicity without an adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale tests.

source.place: Second paragraph, supported cohomology, Hom and global sections, with the first-paragraph support-to-exceptional comparison; returned steps 7-9.

proof.text: Apply the shift equivalence to $\phi$ to obtain $C_0\cong C$. Applying cohomology carries degree-zero concentration and the constant rank-one sheaf to $C$. Finite-Tor constructibility is invariant under derived isomorphism: constructible cohomology is unchanged, and tensoring an isomorphism with any degree-zero module sheaf preserves each cohomological vanishing bound. Thus $C\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, by the defining condition of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

source.place: Second paragraph, supported cohomology, Hom and global sections, with the first-paragraph support-to-exceptional comparison; returned steps 7-9.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-supported-hom] to the bounded-below $K$ with $a=2$. Exact termwise $i_*$ commutes with shifts, giving $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*A_Z,K[2])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*(A_Z[-2]),K)$. Apply the support adjunction of [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle], shift both arguments, and postcompose with $\phi[2]$. Every map in this chain is a bijection, yielding precisely $\eta$ with the formula in the statement. The object $A_Z[-2]$ has the etale origin exhibited in step 2, so the agreement of adjunctions proved in step 3 applies to this test. Therefore this formula is also the relative exceptional transpose.

source.place: Second paragraph, supported cohomology, Hom and global sections, with the first-paragraph support-to-exceptional comparison; returned steps 7-9.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization] in the abelian category of $A_Z$-module sheaves to $A_Z[0]$ and $C$, both concentrated in degree zero by step 4. It gives the canonical $t_C:C\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^0(C)[0]$ and the bijection $m\mapsto\mathcal H^0(m)$ from derived morphisms to module-sheaf maps $A_Z\to\mathcal H^0(C)$. Evaluation at $1$ is a bijection on these sheaf maps: its inverse sends $v\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal H^0(C))$ to $f_{v,W}(a)=a\,v|_W$ on every site object $W$. Restrictions commute with multiplication, so this is a module-sheaf map; $f_{v,Z}(1)=v$, and any module map $f$ satisfies $f_W(a)=a f_W(1)=a f_Z(1)|_W$. Hence the inverse of $\mathrm{ev}$ is $v\mapsto t_C^{-1}\circ f_v[0]$, exactly as asserted. This elementary evaluation calculation uses the module morphisms of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; the derived-to-sheaf passage uses the cited truncation theorem.

source.place: Second paragraph, supported cohomology, Hom and global sections, with the first-paragraph support-to-exceptional comparison; returned steps 7-9.

proof.text: By [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], $\beta=\partial\alpha$ lies in $H^2_Z(X,K)$. For $m=\eta(\beta)$, substitution gives $\mathrm{ev}(m)=(\mathrm{ev}\circ\eta)(\beta)$. The two maps are bijective by steps 5 and 6, so applying their composite inverse gives $(\mathrm{ev}\eta)^{-1}(\mathrm{ev}(m))=\beta$. Inverting this composite is the claimed canonical isomorphism from global sections to supported cohomology.
